Method of Attack: Injected directly into the memory of Cisco routers running older firmware versions
Provides unauthenticated backdoor access to the device
Exploits the patched SNMP vulnerability CVE-2017-6742
Scans for public Cisco routers using weak SNMP community strings
Patches router memory to install non-persistent malware
Grants access to existing local accounts without password verification via Telnet or physical session
Creates a process to collect CLI command outputs and exfiltrates data using TFTP
Discoverer: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
Impacted Systems: Cisco IOS routers running firmware C5350-ISM, Version 12.3(6)
Attack Vector: Use of weak SNMP community strings such as 'public' to gain access
